items.title: Section: The Abode Joined With the Truths Opens — the Fifth Ground

items.zh: 云何菩薩諸諦相應增上慧住？
items.en: Sixth abode, joined with the truths; first, the question. What is a bodhisattva's abode joined with the truths?

items.title: Section: Ten Kinds of Equally Purified Aspiration — Past, Present, and Future Buddha-Dharma All Equal

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，先於覺分相應增上慧住，已得十種平等清淨意樂。由彼平等清淨意樂成上品故，極圓滿故，超過第一增上慧住，證入第二增上慧住。十種平等清淨意樂所有文詞，如契經說，應知其相。
items.en:
First aspect: entry brought to fulfilment through equally purified aspiration; first, clarifying entry. Namely, bodhisattvas, previously at the abode joined with the factors of awakening, have already attained ten kinds of equally purified aspiration. By this equally purified aspiration becoming of the most excellent grade, utterly complete, one passes beyond the first abode of heightened wisdom and enters the second.
Second, pointing to what the sutra says. The wording of these ten kinds of equally purified aspiration is exactly as the sutra explains; one should understand their mark accordingly.
Commentary: Regarding "the wording of these ten kinds" and the like — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: if a bodhisattva, having attained the fourth bodhisattva ground and its well-fulfilled conduct, wishes to enter the fifth bodhisattva ground, should enter by ten kinds of deeply pure, equal mind. What are the ten? First, a deeply pure mind of equality regarding past buddha-dharma. Second, regarding future buddha-dharma. Third, regarding present buddha-dharma. Fourth, regarding purity of precept. Fifth, regarding purity of mind. Sixth, regarding purity removing view, doubt, and regret. Seventh, regarding purity of the wisdom distinguishing path from non-path. Eighth, regarding purity of the wisdom of conduct and its severance. Ninth, regarding ever-higher purity in contemplating every factor of awakening. Tenth, regarding purity in transforming and liberating every sentient being.

items.title: Section: Equal Awakening and Every Method of Awakening, Both Held Without Discrimination — Closing the First Aspect

items.zh: 謂無等覺與諸覺等，超過所餘諸有情界及以諸法，如其平等。當知是名十種平等清淨意樂略所說義。
items.en:
Third, clarifying the brief meaning. Without discrimination towards equal awakening and every method of awakening, surpassing every remaining realm of sentient beings and every dharma, exactly according with equality — one should understand this as the brief meaning of these ten kinds of equally purified aspiration.
Commentary: Regarding "without equal awakening" and the like — the sutra says: a deeply pure mind of equality regarding past, future, and present buddha-dharma is exactly this "without equal awakening." The sutra says: the remaining purity of precept, mind, on through purity in transforming and liberating every sentient being is exactly this "without every method of awakening." Because all these minds accord with every buddha-dharma, gathering everything together, they are called "every method of awakening." Because no discrimination arises regarding either equal awakening or every method of awakening, this is called "without" — thereby surpassing pride connected with a sense of self and pride connected with a sense of dharmas. Genuinely penetrating that sentient beings and dharmas admit of no increase or decrease is called "exactly according with equality" — this explains why this purified aspiration is named equality.

items.title: Section: Ten Further Aspects for Observing the Four Noble Truths — From Worldly Truth to Gathering the Tathāgata's Own Wisdom

items.zh: 如是菩薩住此住中，多分希求智殊勝性。於四聖諦，由十行相如實了知。一切文詞，如契經說，應知其相。
items.en:
Second aspect: skilful means for observing the truths; first, pointing to what the sutra says. Such bodhisattvas, abiding in this abode, for the most part seek out wisdom's own excellent nature. Regarding the four noble truths, through ten distinct aspects, they genuinely know them; the full wording follows exactly as the sutra explains — one should understand their mark accordingly.
Commentary: Regarding "regarding the four noble truths, through ten distinct aspects" and the like — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: this bodhisattva genuinely knows this is the noble truth of suffering, this is the truth of suffering's origin, this is the truth of suffering's cessation; genuinely knows this is the noble truth of the path to suffering's cessation. This bodhisattva skilfully knows worldly truth, skilfully knows ultimate truth, skilfully knows the truth of characteristics, skilfully knows the truth of distinctions, skilfully knows the truth of how teaching is established, skilfully knows the truth of actual matters, skilfully knows the truth of arising, skilfully knows the truth of the wisdom of cessation without further arising, skilfully knows the truth of the wisdom leading into the path, and skilfully knows the truth of every bodhisattva ground's own sequential accomplishment together with gathering the Tathāgata's own wisdom.

items.title: Section: The Fourfold Restatement — By Whom, By What Source, and For What Purpose the Truths Are Taught

items.zh: 謂依曉悟他、依自內智、依俱處所，名為此說。依於契經、調伏、本母，名由此說。依於現在眾苦自性、依於未來苦因生性、依於因盡彼盡無生性、依於修習彼斷方便性，名如此說。當知是名十種行相四聖諦智所有略義。
items.en:
Second, clarifying the brief meaning. Relying on awakening others, relying on one's own inner wisdom, relying on the two together — this is called "for this reason it is said." Relying on the sutras, the discipline, and the root-treatises — this is called "by this it is said." Relying on the nature of present suffering, relying on the nature giving rise to future suffering's cause, relying on the nature by which, the cause exhausted, suffering too is exhausted without further arising, relying on the nature of the means for cultivating this severance — this is called "explained in just this way." One should understand this as the brief meaning of the ten aspects of wisdom regarding the four noble truths.
Commentary: Regarding "relying on awakening others" and the like — this brief meaning does not restate the ten aspects individually, but is rather the essential meaning of that wisdom as a whole. "Relying on awakening others" is the brief meaning of the ten aspects, since by these all others are matured. "Relying on one's own inner wisdom" is the brief meaning of the four-truths wisdom itself, since by this everything is genuinely known. "Relying on the two together" is the total brief meaning of the ten-aspect four-truths wisdom, since it arises relying on both others and oneself. For the sake of all this, it is therefore proclaimed — this is called "for this reason it is said." As for "the sutras, the discipline, and the root-treatises" — this displays how the buddha's teaching is established through actual matters, since these three together gather in the entirety of every buddha's own teaching; by these three there is what is taught — this is called "by this it is said." As for "relying on the nature of present suffering" and the like — relying on this, the four truths are established in their distinct order; each is proclaimed exactly according to its own nature — this is called "explained in just this way."

items.title: Section: Formations Seen as Deceptive and Empty, and a Vivid Portrait of Beings Who Will Not Flee Their Own Decaying Bodies

items.zh: 如是於諦善巧菩薩，於一切行以慧正毀，於有情界增悲意樂，於前後際愚癡有情所有邪行能正通達。
items.en:
Third aspect: destroying conditioned formations, arousing compassion for sentient beings. A bodhisattva skilled in the truths in this way correctly destroys every conditioned formation through wisdom, increases compassionate aspiration towards the realm of sentient beings, and correctly penetrates the wrongful conduct of beings deluded regarding the prior boundary, the later boundary, and what lies between.
Commentary: Regarding "the wrongful conduct of beings deluded regarding both the prior and later boundary" — this refers to beings ignorant of the prior boundary, ignorant of the later boundary, and ignorant of both together, who, towards conditioned formations, give rise to incorrect discrimination, grasping either at annihilation or at permanence — this is called their wrongful conduct.
The bodhisattva at that time reflects thus: these many ordinary beings are truly strange — foolish, without wisdom, having had immeasurable, boundless bodies already destroyed, being destroyed now, and yet to be destroyed. Having witnessed such complete destruction, they still cannot give rise to any thought of aversion towards the body, instead further increasing the karmic mechanism for yet another suffering body, forever following the world's own current, unable to return; unable to depart from the five-aggregate dwelling, unafraid of the four elements' venomous serpents, unable to draw out the arrow of self-pride and view, unable to extinguish the fire of craving, hatred, and delusion, unable to break through ignorance's own darkness, unable to drain the great river of clinging attachment, not seeking the great, noble guide endowed with the ten powers, constantly entering the dense thicket of demonic intention, forever turned about by every evil deliberation upon the sea of birth and death.

items.title: Section: Vowing to Gather Merit and Wisdom, and Every Excellent Quality Flourishing Under Mindful, Discerning Conduct

items.zh: 為欲令彼得解脫故，攝受廣大福智資糧，心發正願。及即於彼意樂引攝正念慧行而為上首，所有眾多殊勝功德皆悉增盛。
items.en:
Fourth aspect: vowing to gather the provisions of merit and wisdom. In order that beings may attain liberation, gathering vast provisions of merit and wisdom, the mind arouses a correct vow to this effect.
Fifth aspect: mindful, discerning conduct flourishing in excellence. And, precisely within that same aspiration, taking correct mindfulness and discerning conduct as foremost, all the many excellent qualities thereby flourish in abundance.

items.title: Section: Every Other Concern Set Aside — Diligently Maturing Sentient Beings Alone

items.zh: 諸餘作意皆悉遠離。以其種種成熟方便成熟有情。
items.en:
Sixth aspect: no remaining intention, diligently maturing sentient beings. Every other kind of intention is entirely set aside. Through every kind of skilful means for maturation, one matures sentient beings.
Commentary: Regarding "every other kind of intention is entirely set aside" — every inferior intention belonging to hearers and solitary-realisers is called other intention, since both abandon sentient beings.

items.title: Section: Worldly Treatises and the Twelve Crafts Mastered — Logic, Rhetoric, and Medicine; Seals, Reckoning, and the Rest

items.zh: 如契經說：所有種種能益有情世俗書論、印算計等工業明處，於是一切皆能引發；於諸有情深悲愍故，漸次乃至方便安立妙菩提故。
items.en:
Seventh aspect: drawing forth worldly crafts and branches of learning; first, naming the purpose. As the sutra says: whatever worldly writings and treatises, seals, reckoning, and other crafts and branches of learning genuinely benefit sentient beings — all of these, one is able to draw forth.
Commentary: Regarding "worldly writings and treatises" — logical treatises, treatises on rhetoric, and treatises on medicine are called worldly writings and treatises. The crafts and branches of learning number twelve kinds; beyond seals and reckoning, the rest are placed under "and the rest."
Out of deep compassion for sentient beings, gradually, by stages, skilfully establishing them in wondrous awakening.

items.title: Section: Ten Concrete Ways Worldly Mastery Benefits Beings — From Relieving Poverty to Teaching the Undistorted Path of Higher Rebirth

items.zh: 隨順世間言說事故；為欲方便壞貧窮故；為令世間諸界錯亂、人非人等所起災患皆息滅故；為施無罪諸戲樂具，除彼非法諸戲樂故；諸有希求種種居處資生具者，為少用功皆能施與種種居處資生具故；為欲拔濟諸王賊等逼惱事故；為欲開制是處非處諸加行故；為欲安立吉非吉事，令取捨故；為正勸獎，於現法中令其展轉不相謀略，及為宣說當來無倒勝生道故。當知是名能益有情工業明處略所說義。
items.en: Second, clarifying the brief meaning. According with worldly discourse and custom; skilfully breaking the grip of poverty; causing the disturbances and disasters arising from disordered elements, and from non-human and human harm, all to cease; bestowing blameless amusements while removing unlawful ones; for those who seek various dwellings and livelihood-necessities, providing these with minimal effort; rescuing beings from oppression by kings or bandits; skilfully permitting or restraining various undertakings as fitting; correctly establishing what is auspicious and inauspicious, so that beings know what to accept and decline; correctly encouraging beings, in the present life, not to plunder or scheme against one another; and proclaiming, for the world to come, the undistorted path of higher rebirth. One should understand this as the brief meaning of the crafts and branches of learning that benefit sentient beings.

items.title: Section: Gold Now Set With Agate, and Wisdom Like Sun and Moon Moving in Harmony With the Very Wind That Cannot Outshine Them

items.zh: 其餘一切，如前應知。此差別者，謂如世間善巧工匠，以所鍊金作莊嚴具，牟裟羅寶瑩飾廁鈿，所有餘金無與等故，不能映奪。如是此中菩薩善根，一切聲聞及諸獨覺、餘地菩薩不能映奪。又如日月諸宿光明，一切風輪不能映奪，然其迴轉共彼風同。如是此中菩薩妙慧，一切聲聞、諸獨覺等不能映奪，然其所作與世共同。
items.en:
Eighth aspect: purified wholesome roots; first, the general account; first, pointing to what was already said. Everything else follows exactly as already explained.
Second, a simile marking the difference. The difference is this: just as, in the world, a skilful craftsman's own smelted gold, wrought into an ornament and set with agate for brilliant adornment, cannot be equaled by any other gold lacking such adornment — so too this bodhisattva's own wholesome roots cannot be outshone by any hearer, solitary-realiser, or bodhisattva of a lesser ground.
Second, a further simile specifically for the faculty of wisdom. Just as the light of the sun, moon, and constellations cannot be outshone by any wheel of wind, and yet these continue to revolve in harmony with that very wind — so too this bodhisattva's own wondrous wisdom cannot be outshone by any hearer or solitary-realiser, and yet its undertakings proceed in harmony with the world.

items.title: Section: Rebirth as Lord of the Tuṣita Heaven, and Majestic Power Reaching a Thousand Koṭi

items.zh: 受生多作珊覩史多天王，善化有情，令捨一切外道邪法。所有威力，當知此說千俱胝數。
items.en:
Ninth aspect: rebirth. Taking rebirth, one most often becomes the lord of the Tuṣita heaven, skilfully transforming sentient beings, causing them to abandon every kind of non-Buddhist, wrongful teaching.
Tenth aspect: majestic power. One should understand that the majestic power spoken of here reaches a thousand koṭi.

items.title: Section: The Summary Names All Ten Aspects, and the Treatise Confirms — This Is the Ground Hard to Conquer

items.zh: 當知是名略說菩薩諸諦相應增上慧住。謂十平等清淨意樂成滿得入故；善巧方便觀察諸諦漸增長故；毀壞諸行、悲愍有情漸增長故；即為是義，長養廣大福智資糧，心發正願勤加行故；念慧行等德增長故；無餘作意，以一切種成熟有情勤加行故；引發世間工巧業故；善根清淨故；受生故；威力故。若廣宣說，如十地經極難勝地。今此地中，顯示菩薩於諸聖諦決定妙智極難可勝，是故此地名極難勝。即由此義，應知此中諸諦相應增上慧住。
items.en:
Second, closing the brief meaning. One should understand this, in brief, as the bodhisattva's abode joined with the truths — namely, because entry is brought to fulfilment through ten kinds of equally purified aspiration; because skilful means for observing the truths gradually increase; because destroying formations and compassion for sentient beings gradually increase; because, for this very purpose, vast provisions of merit and wisdom are cultivated, the mind diligently arousing a correct vow; because qualities of mindfulness, discernment, and conduct increase; because, with no remaining intention, every kind of skilful means diligently matures sentient beings; because worldly crafts and branches of learning are drawn forth; because of purified wholesome roots; because of rebirth; because of majestic power.
Second, the broader pointer; first, pointing to it. Should one wish to hear it expounded at length, it is exactly as the Ten Grounds Sutra expounds it in its chapter on the ground hard to conquer.
Second, explaining. Within this ground, it is displayed that the bodhisattva's own decisive, wondrous wisdom regarding the noble truths is extremely difficult to surpass; this is why this ground is named the ground hard to conquer.
Third, the correspondence. By this very meaning, one should understand this is exactly the abode joined with the truths spoken of here.

blocks.text: The fifth ground looks at the four noble truths from ten angles, and, surprisingly, it is also the ground where the bodhisattva masters worldly learning: medicine, writing, arithmetic, crafts.

"The flame of true wisdom of the factors of awakening illuminates the teaching: hence Blazing Wisdom." Venerable Miào Jìng: "path" is precepts, concentration, and wisdom; "non-path" is greed, hatred, and delusion.
Venerable Miào Jìng: 無 here means non-discrimination, not giving rise to distinctions. (Ru-Yi's "without equal" contradicts this.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: suffering and its origin are the gate of wandering; cessation and the path the gate of return. The deepest root of suffering is this single deluded, discriminating thought.
"Relying on the sūtras, the discipline, and the root-treatises." Venerable Miào Jìng: for your own practice the four truths suffice; to awaken others you must explain all ten aspects.
Master Cháng Bǎi: call it cut off and it continues; call it permanent and it changes.
Venerable Miào Jìng: with wisdom but no merit, beings won't accept your teaching; with merit, they are won over the moment they see you.
"Every other intention is entirely set aside." Master Cháng Bǎi: the two vehicles seek only their own liberation.

"Out of deep compassion for beings, gradually and skilfully establishing them in wondrous awakening." Master Cháng Bǎi: "first hook them with desire, then lead them into buddha-wisdom." Venerable Miào Jìng: once livelihood is solved, then the factors of awakening and the perfections.
Both lecturers: 牟娑羅 is agate, set into the gold as decoration.
A bodhisattva on the fifth ground studies medicine and arithmetic. Practical help is not a distraction from the path; at this stage it is the path.

quiz.q: What is the fourth abode called in the Ten Grounds Sūtra, and why?
options: Blazing Wisdom — the flame of true wisdom of the factors of awakening illuminates the teaching
quiz.why: "In this ground the flame of true wisdom of the factors of awakening illuminates the teaching — hence Blazing Wisdom." Master Cháng Bǎi: wisdom strong as a flame.

quiz.q: Among the ten, "purity of knowing path and non-path." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain these?
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "path" is precepts, concentration, and wisdom; "non-path" is greed, hatred, and delusion; "purity of precepts" is precepts, "purity of mind" concentration.

quiz.q: "無等覺與諸覺等" — the English title reads "Awakening Without Equal." How do the lectures read 無?
options: both: 無 means non-discrimination, applying to both "equal awakening" and "methods of awakening"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "無" means non-discrimination, and it carries through to "methods of awakening." Venerable Miào Jìng: 無 means non-discrimination — not giving rise to distinctions. The English "without equal" contradicts this.

quiz.q: The fifth-ground bodhisattva seeks excellent wisdom, knowing the truths in ten aspects. What does Master Cháng Bǎi say is the root of suffering?
options: the root is this single deluded discriminating thought; suffering and origin are the gate of wandering, cessation and path the gate of return
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: suffering and its origin are the gate of wandering, cessation and path the gate of return; the deepest root of suffering is this single deluded, discriminating thought. Venerable Miào Jìng agrees.

quiz.q: "Relying on 契經, 調伏, 本母." What are these?
quiz.why: "Relying on the sūtras, the discipline, and the root-treatises." Both lecturers: sūtra, vinaya, abhidharma.

quiz.q: Why, according to Venerable Miào Jìng, are the truths explained in ten aspects?
options: for one's own practice the four truths suffice, but to awaken others the ten aspects are needed
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: for your own practice the four truths suffice; but to awaken others you must explain the ten aspects. Master Cháng Bǎi: buddhas and bodhisattvas also learn — otherwise how could they teach?

quiz.q: "Beings deluded about 前後際." How does Venerable Miào Jìng read it? The English says "prior and later boundary."
options: "前後際" is the present — after the past, before the future
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "前後際" is the present — after the prior boundary and before the later one. Master Cháng Bǎi: call it cut off and it continues; call it permanent and it changes — neither annihilation nor permanence.

quiz.q: "Gathering vast provisions of merit and wisdom." Why must merit be cultivated, according to the lectures?
options: both: with enough merit beings will listen; Miào Jìng: wisdom without merit and beings won't accept you — with merit they're won over before you speak
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: only with sufficient merit will beings listen. Venerable Miào Jìng: with wisdom but no merit, beings won't accept your teaching; with merit, they're won over the moment they see you.

quiz.q: "Every other intention is set aside." What is "other intention"?
options: the inferior intentions of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, who seek only their own liberation and abandon beings
quiz.why: "Every other intention is entirely set aside; through every means one matures beings." Master Cháng Bǎi: the two vehicles seek only their own liberation, abandoning beings.

quiz.q: The fifth-ground bodhisattva draws forth worldly crafts — for what ultimate purpose?
options: out of deep compassion, gradually establishing beings in wondrous awakening
quiz.why: "Out of deep compassion for beings, gradually and skilfully establishing them in wondrous awakening." Master Cháng Bǎi: "first hook them with desire, then lead them into buddha-wisdom." Venerable Miào Jìng: once livelihood is solved, then the factors of awakening and perfections.

quiz.q: The fifth-ground simile — gold "set with 牟娑羅 jewels." How do the lectures explain it?
options: both: 牟娑羅 is agate, adorning the gold; Miào Jìng adds 鈿 are gold flowers
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 牟娑羅 is agate, used to adorn the gold. Venerable Miào Jìng: 牟娑羅 translates as agate; 鈿 are gold flowers set on it.
